summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD s/p CABG, COPD, GERD, chronic esophagitis, and alcohol abuse was admitted after experiencing severe epigastric and chest pain following a large greasy meal and alcohol consumption. He described the pain as sharp and pressure-like, worse than typical heartburn, prompting him to call for help. Initial evaluation included cardiac monitoring, negative troponins x3, and an EKG showing no acute changes, ruling out myocardial infarction. Imaging revealed gastric dilatation with no evidence of pneumonia or heart failure. Pain improved with morphine, antacids, and nitroglycerin. He was managed for alcohol intoxication with IV fluids, thiamine, and folate, and monitored for withdrawal without complications. Due to baseline dysphagia and aspiration risk, he was kept NPO initially and evaluated by speech therapy before advancing to soft diet. His acidosis resolved with hydration, and anemia was attributed to hemodilution. By discharge, he was pain-free, tolerating oral intake, and stable vitally. He was discharged home with services, new ranitidine prescription, and follow-up plans for substance abuse counseling and primary care.
